title: Join All the Points With the Least Cable

concept.title: Prim's algorithm on a complete graph: grow one tree, always adding the closest outside point
body: There are `n` points on a plane. Joining two points costs the **Manhattan distance** `|x1 - x2| + |y1 - y2|`. Connect all the points with the smallest total cost. Every pair of points can be joined, so the graph is *complete*: it has `n * (n - 1) / 2` edges, almost half a million for `n = 1000`. Writing all edges down and sorting them (Kruskal) works, but there is a method that does not need the edge list.

*Prim's algorithm* grows a single tree from one point. Keep for every point outside the tree the **cheapest connection to the tree** so far (`best[v]`). Repeat `n` times: take the outside point with the smallest `best` (scan all points, O(n)), add it to the tree (add its `best` to the total), and then update `best` of the other outside points with their distance to the new point.

body.code:
best = [INF] * n
used = [False] * n
best[0] = 0
total = 0
for _ in range(n):
    u = min((v for v in range(n) if not used[v]), key=lambda v: best[v])   # the closest outside point
    used[u] = True
    total += best[u]
    for v in range(n):
        if not used[v]:
            best[v] = min(best[v], abs(x[u] - x[v]) + abs(y[u] - y[v]))

body: With a scan instead of a heap the time is O(n^2), which is just right for a complete graph (a heap would not help, since all `n^2` edges must be looked at anyway). The sum can reach 4 * 10^9, so use 64-bit integers.

statement: `n` points are given on a plane. Joining two points costs the sum of the absolute differences of their coordinates, `|x1 - x2| + |y1 - y2|`. Print the smallest total cost of joinings such that all points are connected to each other (directly or through other points).
inputFormat: The first line has `n`, the number of points.
Each of the next `n` lines has two numbers `x` and `y`: the coordinates of a point.
hints: Keep for every point not yet in the tree the cheapest distance to the tree.
Repeat n times: take the closest such point, add its cost, and update the others with their distance to it.
The scan makes the whole algorithm O(n^2).

explanation: Prim's algorithm with a scan: the closest point outside the tree is added in every round, and the cheapest connections of the other points are updated with their distance to it.

code.python:
import sys
input = sys.stdin.readline

n = int(input())
pts = [list(map(int, input().split())) for _ in range(n)]

INF = 10 ** 18
best = [INF] * n
used = [False] * n
best[0] = 0
total = 0
for _ in range(n):
    u = -1
    for v in range(n):
        if not used[v] and (u == -1 or best[v] < best[u]):
            u = v
    used[u] = True
    total += best[u]
    ux, uy = pts[u]
    for v in range(n):
        if not used[v]:
            d = abs(ux - pts[v][0]) + abs(uy - pts[v][1])
            if d < best[v]:
                best[v] = d
print(total)
